---
title: "Data volume and precision"
subtitle: "How the files are kept small, and what that means for the values in them"
---

FesmData puts many datasets on many grids, from 25 m to 5°. To keep the
releases small enough to download and store, every file is made with the measures below.
None of them changes how the files are read: they are ordinary NetCDF-4 files with
Float32 and integer variables.

## Resolution

A thematic dataset (GHF, SMB, Velocity, ...) is made only on grids that add information:
as a rule, no grid is finer than about a quarter of the spacing of its source, e.g. 16 km
and 0.5° for sources at 1-2°, 8 km and 0.25° for sources at 0.25-0.5°, 4 km for most
others (`grids` of a product, see [Bring your own data](remap.qmd#make-a-thematic-dataset)).
A finer grid of a coarse source would only be large; a model that needs it can remap
online. Topo and Regions, made from high-resolution sources, are on all grids.

## Crops and nests

The crops of a domain (e.g. Greenland, Laurentide, Eurasia, NorthPatagonianIcefield) and
its nests (e.g. SRG) lie on the grids of their parent. Their thematic datasets are
therefore not stored: `fetch` cuts the product of the parent to them on demand (see
[Nests and crops](download.qmd#nests-and-crops)). Only a product made for the crop or nest itself
(e.g. a Greenland-only source on Greenland) is stored there.

## Precision

Each float field is rounded on output to a tolerance that depends on its kind, well
below the uncertainty of the data: the mantissa bits of each value that are not needed
for that tolerance are set to zero (bit rounding), which compresses much better. The
values stay Float32, and missing values are kept.

| Kind of field | Recognised by | Tolerance |
|---|---|---|
| Longitude, latitude (`lon2D`, `lat2D`) | name, or units `degrees_east`, `degrees_north` | lossless |
| Cell area (`area`) | name | 1e-5 relative (0.001%) |
| Fractions (`f_ice`, `f_valid`, cloud cover, albedo, ...) | name `f_*`, or units `1` | 0.001 |
| Ice velocities (`ux_srf`, `uy_srf`, `uxy_srf` and their errors) | name `ux`, `uy`, `uz`, `uxy`, and units `m yr-1` | 1% or 1 m yr-1, the larger |
| Rates (`smb`, `pr`, `sf`, `rf`, `melt`, `runoff`, `subl`, `bmelt`, ...) | name | 1% |
| Elevations, thicknesses, depths (`z_*`, `H_*`, their `*_sd`, ...) | units `m` | 0.01 m |
| Temperatures | units `K`, `degC` | 0.01 K |
| Other rates and fluxes (`dzdt`, winds, `ghf`, radiation, ...) | units per time (`yr-1`, `s-1`, `d-1`), or `W m-2` | 1% |
| Everything else (salinity, viscosity, ages, distances in km, ...) | | 3 significant digits (0.05%) |

The first row that matches a field applies (`shared/precision.jl`). A domain may set
another tolerance of elevations and thicknesses (`elevation_precision` in
`shared/domains.toml`); none does. Integer fields
(masks, classes, region numbers) are never rounded. A relative tolerance holds for each
value; for an absolute tolerance, the bits kept are set by the largest magnitude of the
field, so that every value is within it; most errors are well below the tolerance. The
coarser Topo grids and the ensemble products are made from rounded files and rounded
again, so their error can exceed the tolerance slightly. Intermediate files of the
pipelines are not rounded.

The precision of each field is in its attributes:

```
float z_bed(yc, xc) ;
        z_bed:units = "m" ;
        z_bed:precision = "0.01 m" ;
        z_bed:bitround_keepbits = 15 ;
```

`precision` is the tolerance (`"0.01 m"`, `"1%"`, `"1% or 1 m yr-1"`, `"lossless"`),
`bitround_keepbits` the mantissa bits kept (of 23; 23 is lossless).

With the rounding, the fields are compressed with deflate level 4 (with shuffle) instead
of level 1. Measured on Levante against the earlier files (lossless, level 1), the files
are smaller by:

| Files | Factor |
|---|---|
| Topo | 1.4-1.5 |
| Regions | 4.6 |
| Velocity | 3.3 |
| SMB | 3.9 |
| Atmosphere (ERA5) | 3.4 |
| Paleoclimate (Buizert2018) | 2.4 |
| Grid files | 1.4 |

Writing is as fast or faster. Deflate level 9 gained too little to be worth it.

A field that needs a finer precision (or allows a coarser one) gets an exception in its
product: `precision` in `<Dataset>/remap.toml` (see
[Bring your own data](remap.qmd#make-a-thematic-dataset)), e.g.
`precision = { ghf = 0.1, smb = "1%", lat = "lossless" }`. If you need one, open an
issue.

## Inactive domains

Domains that are defined but not used yet (e.g. Alps, Svalbard, New Zealand, and some
nests of the ice sheets)
are inactive: their grids and products are made only on request, and they are left out
of the releases (see [Domains and grids](domains.qmd#domains)).

## Releases

Only the latest release of each dataset is kept on Helmholtz Codebase. Earlier releases
still in use are kept in archives on the HPC systems (`mirror --dir`, see
[Archives and other folders](download.qmd#archives-and-other-folders)).
